title: Security posture discovery with Ventus Analytics
next_steps: Send SOC 2 Type II evidence and ISO summary
Share SSO/SAML configuration guide and sample metadata XML
Schedule architecture deep dive with Ventus infra (week of 12/22)
Provide draft pricing for Hosted vs Dedicated with BYOK option
action_items: Maya Chen: Send SOC2 report and security pack by 2025-12-19
Liam O'Connor: Prepare sample SAML metadata and RBAC mapping doc by 2025-12-20
Marcus Lee: Share Ventus encryption/KMS requirements and key lifecycle doc by 2025-12-22
header:
Date: 2025-12-18
Time: 15:00 - 15:42 UTC
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood SE), Priya Rao (Ventus - Head of ML), Marcus Lee (Ventus - Security Engineer), Oliver Grant (Ventus - CTO)
summary: Discovery-style security posture call focused on hosted vs dedicated/private deployment choices. Ventus is evaluating Redwood for inference hosting; primary concerns are SOC2/ISO compliance, SSO/SAML integration, RBAC and least-privilege, audit logs retention and export, encryption and KMS/BYOK, and data residency/retention policies. AE/SE explained Redwood Hosted, Dedicated, and Private options and fallback patterns; agreed to share SOC2 artifacts, SAML config, and schedule a deeper architecture session to validate BYOK and network/VPC requirements.
topics: Encryption at rest/in transit and KMS/BYOK
Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private deployment tradeoffs
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for carving out time, appreciate it. We're Maya from Redwood, and Liam's with me from our security and infra team.
[00:12] Priya Rao: Hi Maya, hi Liam. Thanks. We're excited to dig in. Quick context, Ventus is moving inference off of a self-hosted prototype to something more production-ready, we want to understand security posture before we pick hosted vs dedicated.
[00:25] Liam O'Connor: Great. Today we can run through SOC2/ISO, SSO, RBAC, audit logging, encryption and KMS, plus data residency and retention. Happy to surface what each deployment mode gives you.
[00:38] Oliver Grant: Awesome. Timebox is 40 minutes, we'll try to cover the checklist.
[00:45] Marcus Lee: And I'll be the primary VM on security questions. We have compliance requirements for our platform customers, need to show our vendors have SOC2 Type II, and ideally ISO 27001.
[00:58] Maya Chen: Totally, Ventus is similar to other fintech and health customers we talk to. We are SOC2 Type II, cert is available, and we're in process with an ISO self assessment — should be able to share a summary. We'll send the SOC2 report redacted.
[01:15] Priya Rao: When you say "send", is that the standard redacted PDF you provide to customers? We need details on controls around data encryption and key management.
[01:26] Maya Chen: Yes, redacted SOC2 PDF. For KMS we support both Redwood-managed keys and customer-managed keys (BYOK) via standard KMS integrations.
[01:36] Marcus Lee: BYOK is a must for us for dedicated/private. We need control of key rotation and offboarding. How does Redwood do key lifecycle and HSM requirement?
[01:49] Liam O'Connor: Good question. For Hosted with BYOK we integrate with customer KMS providers — we can do AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and Azure Key Vault. Keys are never exported from the KMS; Redwood performs envelope encryption. For Dedicated and Private you can bring keys into an HSM if required, and we can support customer-managed HSMs in the VPC deployment.
[02:10] Marcus Lee: When you say "envelope encryption", can you expand? Sometimes transcriptions or logs leak key identifiers. We need to ensure no plaintext model inputs/outputs are written to logs.
[02:24] Liam O'Connor: Envelope encryption means we encrypt data with a data key that is itself encrypted by your KMS master key. Logs redact sensitive fields by default; audit logs include metadata (request id, model, latency) but not full prompt text unless you enable long-term storage for debugging.
[02:41] Marcus Lee: Who has access to those logs, and is there RBAC to restrict access?
[02:47] Maya Chen: Yes, we have role-based access control (RBAC) at the org/team/token level. Admins can see broader telemetry; developers can see request traces for their tokens. For Dedicated and Private you can restrict access to safety teams or SRE only.
[03:04] Priya Rao: We use Okta as our IdP. Does Redwood support SAML? SSO? SCIM provisioning?
[03:11] Liam O'Connor: We support SSO via SAML and OIDC; SCIM for user provisioning is supported for Dedicated and Private deployments today and planned for Hosted in the next quarter. We'll share a SAML metadata XML and example setup guide.
[03:28] Oliver Grant: Can you do automatic role mapping from Okta groups to Redwood roles?
[03:34] Maya Chen: Yes, group mapping is supported — you'll map Okta groups to roles like admin, developer, auditor. There can be a custom mapping layer in Dedicated/Private.
[03:43] Marcus Lee: Audit trails: retention and export. We have regulatory requirements to retain certain logs for 7 years, and ability to export to our SIEM.
[03:53] Liam O'Connor: Our standard audit log retention for Hosted is 90 days for operational dashboards; exports to external storage (S3, GCS) and streaming to SIEM via syslog/forwarder are available for Dedicated and Private. For Hosted enterprise customers we can negotiate longer retention or push logs to a customer-owned bucket.
[04:12] Priya Rao: Are request/response bodies ever part of those logs by default? We don't want any PII or customer data stored in any long-term location.
[04:21] Maya Chen: No, by default payloads are not stored long-term. Short-term traces for debugging exist for a configurable retention window and are redacted unless you enable a debug mode. We'll send the debug-mode policy and how to opt-in.
[04:34] Marcus Lee: Ok, billing data is fine, but payload content must be excluded unless explicitly approved.
[04:39] Maya Chen: Understood — that's default behavior.
[04:42] Priya Rao: Network isolation — if we go Dedicated or Private, do you support placing Redwood nodes in our VPC and controlling egress?
[04:51] Liam O'Connor: For Dedicated we offer VPC peering or private link options and we have strict egress controls. For Private on-prem we ship a customer-managed control plane option; that can be air-gapped with periodic metadata sync.
[05:05] Oliver Grant: What about model artifacts and caching — is the model stored in a shared pool? Any risk of cross-tenant leakage?
[05:14] Liam O'Connor: Models are per-customer in Dedicated and Private. For Hosted we run verified model variants; we logically separate cache and KV cache entries per tenant. There's strict namespacing to avoid cross-tenant key collisions. We can provide our architecture whitepaper on KV cache isolation.
[05:31] Marcus Lee: Sometimes transcripts of prompted data end up in block storage or backups. Do you have guaranteed data deletion timelines and proof of deletion?
[05:41] Maya Chen: We have documented data retention and deletion processes. For Hosted we can request data purge and provide attestation within a standard SLA window; for Dedicated and Private you control backups and purge processes directly. We'll include the deletion flow in the docs we send.
[05:58] Priya Rao: For SOC2, do you have the auditor listed and the date of the last audit? We need the control set and if any exceptions were noted.
[06:07] Maya Chen: Yes, SOC2 Type II audited by an external Big Four firm last quarter, no material exceptions. We'll redact customer names and send the cover letter and controls matrix.
[06:20] Oliver Grant: Encryption in transit — TLS? Any mTLS for service-to-service?
[06:25] Liam O'Connor: TLS 1.2/1.3 everywhere; mutual TLS is supported for service endpoints in Dedicated/Private. For Hosted we support mTLS for private links and can provision certs via customer CA if required.
[06:40] Marcus Lee: Does Redwood support hardware-backed key attestation or HSM certified modules like FIPS 140-2/3?
[06:48] Liam O'Connor: Yes, for HSM we can integrate with FIPS-validated HSMs in Dedicated/Private and some BYOK flows for Hosted tie into cloud provider HSM offerings. We'll include the HSM support matrix in the pack.
[07:02] Priya Rao: Are there any pen test reports or bug bounty program details?
[07:07] Maya Chen: We run regular internal and third-party pen tests; we have a public security program for responsible disclosure. We'll include a summary and dates of the most recent tests.
[07:18] Oliver Grant: On compliance mapping, do you offer a controls matrix mapping to SOC2/ISO/GPCI?
[07:25] Maya Chen: We provide a controls mapping doc that shows how Redwood controls map to SOC2 and ISO 27001 clauses; PCI scope is narrower but we can discuss specific cardholder data flows.
[07:36] Priya Rao: Performance and latency — security folks will ask about sidechannel risks and kernel-level isolation. Any mitigations for multi-tenant GPUs?
[07:46] Liam O'Connor: For Hosted we use strong tenant isolation at the process and container boundary; for Dedicated you get single-tenant node pools. We also use mitigations for speculative execution risks and keep hypervisor patches up to date as part of our patching cadence.
[08:04] Marcus Lee: Can you document patch windows and maintenance windows? We need to schedule around our own release calendar.
[08:12] Maya Chen: Sure — production maintenance windows are documented and we can set blackout windows for Dedicated customers. We'll add that to the next pack.
[08:22] Oliver Grant: SLA — uptime and latency SLOs?
[08:26] Liam O'Connor: Hosted SLA varies by tier; enterprise hosted customers get an uptime SLA and latency targets. Dedicated has contractual SLAs with credits for missed targets. We'll share the SLA draft.
[08:36] Priya Rao: Data residency — our customers are EU-only, we need EU data residency and EU-only processing.
[08:44] Maya Chen: We have EU regions for Hosted and can route traffic to EU-only clusters. For Dedicated/Private you can host entirely in EU regions or on-prem. We'll capture the region requirements in the follow-up.
[08:56] Marcus Lee: For the SAML config, can you provide sample metadata and how group claims map to RBAC?
[09:03] Liam O'Connor: Yes, sample metadata and a mapping example will be included. For Hosted the mapping UI is in the console; for Dedicated/Private it's a configuration file we manage with your infra team.
[09:18] Priya Rao: Ok, a couple of tradeoffs: Hosted is quickest to onboard, but we lose some control; Dedicated gives us more control but higher cost and longer lead time. We need recommendations on a pilot approach.
[09:32] Maya Chen: Most customers start Hosted with BYOK for key control and then move to Dedicated when throughput or network isolation needs grow. For Ventus — if BYOK + region controls satisfy compliance, Hosted pilot is fastest. If you require full VPC isolation or HSM certs, start with Dedicated.
[09:50] Oliver Grant: What about cost modelling — per-token vs reserved capacity?
[09:54] Liam O'Connor: Hosted is usage-based per token/embedding. Dedicated is reserved GPU capacity with commit pricing; we can provide a model comparing current TCO across 12 months. We'll run a simple cost calc for your workload in the next session.
[10:07] Marcus Lee: We expect steady throughput of 200 qps peak, with 5k tokens per second sustained in some windows. Will Redwood Dedicated support that?
[10:18] Liam O'Connor: Yes — Dedicated supports predictable throughput and autoscaling policies. We'll need to see exact model size and sequence distributions to size properly; we'll ask for sample traffic patterns and prompts.
[10:28] Priya Rao: Any limits on request size, max sequence?
[10:31] Liam O'Connor: Depends on model profile; we can support up to 8k tokens for certain variants, but higher lengths need special profiling. We'll include model profiles in the pack.
[10:45] Maya Chen: For the pilot, next steps we propose: 1) we'll send SOC2, ISO summary, pen-test summary, and HSM matrix; 2) Liam will share SAML metadata and RBAC mapping examples; 3) Ventus to share a short traffic sample and security questionnaire answers.
[11:02] Oliver Grant: Sounds good. Any blockers from your side on us running a POC on Hosted with BYOK?
[11:09] Liam O'Connor: No blockers. We typically provision a trial org, configure SSO, and enable BYOK with a test KMS key. We'll do an architecture call to validate network flows before you send any customer data.
[11:23] Marcus Lee: What about legal — do you have standard DPA and data processing terms? We need to review data processor obligations.
[11:31] Maya Chen: Yes, we have DPA templates and standard data processing addenda. For enterprise deals we can negotiate specific clauses. We'll attach the DPA and dataflow diagrams.
[11:45] Priya Rao: Ok, I have one last technical: can you restrict token-level costs and limit who can generate long traces?
[11:53] Maya Chen: Yes — there are token-level quotas and per-token cost attribution in the console; trace generation is gated and audited.
[12:02] Oliver Grant: Thanks, that's helpful. Let's recap the action items.
[12:07] Maya Chen: Recap: we'll send SOC2/ISO summary, pen test summary, HSM matrix; Liam to send SAML metadata and RBAC mapping; we'll propose a pilot plan for Hosted with BYOK and draft pricing; Ventus to send traffic sample and security questionnaire.
[12:24] Priya Rao: Great. Can we get the SOC2 by tomorrow? We need to review with compliance.
[12:29] Maya Chen: Yes, we'll send the redacted SOC2 by end of day tomorrow.
[12:33] Marcus Lee: I'll share our KMS policy and requirements doc by the 22nd.
[12:37] Oliver Grant: We'll schedule the architecture deep dive for the week of 12/22.
[12:42] Maya Chen: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up in an email with links and calendar invites.
[12:47] Priya Rao: Thanks. Bye.
[12:50] (call ends)

Note: transcript has occasional mis-hearings and some speaker label drift; timestamps approximate.
